content_html:
Second Brain

One memory for every AI app you use.

Website · Open the app · Security · License: AGPL-3.0

Linked markdown notes that every AI app can read and write. Connect Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI or any MCP client to one remote MCP address, https://mcp.getsecondbrain.io/mcp, save something in one app, and find it from another. Notes live in a workspace you can see as a network and edit in the browser.

This repository is the full source of the hosted service at getsecondbrain.io.

What it does

  • One memory for every AI app. A remote MCP server with OAuth. You pick a workspace and read or read-and-write access when you connect an app, and you can disconnect it at any time.
  • Linked notes. Obsidian-style [[wikilinks]], tags and frontmatter, with backlinks, renames that rewrite links, revisions, a trash and full-text search.
  • Network view. Every note and link drawn as a live graph in the browser.
  • Skills. Notes under Skills/ in the SKILL.md shape become reusable instructions your apps can list and load (list_skills, use_skill, and MCP prompts).
  • Sources. Granola meeting notes sync in hourly.
  • Safe by default for AI writes. Every write is attributed to the app and versioned. Apps can move a note to the trash but never delete it for good; only you can, in the web app.

MCP tools: search, get_note, list_recent, get_linked, list_tags, save_note, update_note, append_to_note, link_notes, trash_note, list_skills, use_skill.

How it is built

One Cloudflare Worker serves four things by hostname: the landing site, the web app and its JSON API, the OAuth server, and the MCP endpoint.

Part Where
Router, security headers src/worker/index.ts
Google sign-in, OAuth server, consent page src/worker/auth/
MCP server and tools src/worker/mcp/
Workspace store: one SQLite Durable Object per workspace (notes, revisions, links, tags, FTS5, audit) src/worker/workspace/
Accounts and memberships (D1) src/worker/control/, migrations/
Sources (Granola sync) src/worker/sources/
Landing site src/worker/site/
Web app (React, sigma.js, CodeMirror 6) src/web/

A workspace id only ever comes from a verified session or OAuth token, never from a request parameter, and every route and tool has a test that one workspace cannot reach another.

Run it locally

Requires Node 24 and pnpm.

pnpm install
pnpm test        # all tests, in the Workers runtime
pnpm dev         # builds the web app and starts the Worker on port 8787

Locally the app is at http://localhost:8787, the MCP endpoint at http://127.0.0.1:8787/mcp and the landing site at http://www.localhost:8787.

Sign-in needs a Google OAuth web client with the redirect URI http://localhost:8787/auth/google/callback. Put the local secrets in .dev.vars (never commit it):

GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=...
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=...
ALLOWED_EMAILS=you@example.com
SOURCES_KEY=...   # openssl rand -base64 32; only needed for Granola

SIGNUP in wrangler.jsonc controls who can join: "open" lets any verified Google account in; any other value allows only ALLOWED_EMAILS.

Deploy your own

  1. Create a D1 database and a KV namespace, then put their ids, your account_id, your hostnames and your origins in the production section of wrangler.jsonc.
  2. Set the secrets: wrangler secret put GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID --env production, and the same for GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, ALLOWED_EMAILS and SOURCES_KEY.
  3. Run pnpm check (types, tests, build, deploy dry run), then pnpm deploy:production, which builds the web app, applies D1 migrations and deploys.

Fair-use limits per workspace (notes, storage, saves a day) are in src/worker/workspace/limits.ts.

Contributing

Issues and pull requests are welcome. See CONTRIBUTING.md and the Code of Conduct.

Security

Please report vulnerabilities privately; see SECURITY.md.

License
